<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="כסלו_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518915911_theRebbe_364" batchId="meluket-_D7_9B_D7_A1_D7_9C_D7_95_meluket__BH_POST_1766518915911_theRebbe_364__p005">
  <section v="12">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Oil's concealment is higher than that of water, as oil is unfit for drinking entirely, representing a concealment beyond revelation.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And one may add,</t>
    <t s="1">that this matter of the concealment of oil</t>
    <t s="2">(which is unfit for drinking)</t>
    <t s="3">is more elevated even than the concealment of water, which has no taste</t>
    <t s="4">(as discussed above in sections 3-4).</t>
    <t s="5">For water,</t>
    <t s="6">although it has no taste,</t>
    <t s="7">is fit for drinking.</t>
    <t s="8">And beyond this,</t>
    <t s="9">it is even possible to derive pleasure from it</t>
    <t s="10">(except that in order to derive pleasure from it, a person must have a sensation of lack</t>
    <t s="11">(thirst)).</t>
    <t s="12">But oil,</t>
    <t s="13">(when it is by itself)</t>
    <t s="14">is not only something from which one cannot derive pleasure, but it is entirely unfit for drinking,</t>
    <t s="15">because it is a level of concealment that is above revelation.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="13">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The distinction between wine, water, and oil corresponds to their spiritual levels: wine is Binah, water is Chochmah, and oil is Chochmah S timaah, which is above revelation.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And it may be said,</t>
    <t s="1">that this distinction between wine, water, and oil</t>
    <t s="2">[for wine has taste,</t>
    <t s="3">water has no taste</t>
    <t s="4">(but is fit for drinking)</t>
    <t s="5">and oil is unfit for drinking]</t>
    <t s="6">corresponds to their spiritual meaning.</t>
    <t s="7">For wine is Binah,</t>
    <t s="8">and therefore it has taste</t>
    <t s="9">(understanding and comprehension),</t>
    <t s="10">water is Chochmah</t>
    <t s="11">(which is above understanding and comprehension),</t>
    <t s="12">and therefore it has no taste,</t>
    <t s="13">but nevertheless it is fit for drinking, and even one can derive pleasure from it,</t>
    <t s="14">because it is revealed Chochmah,</t>
    <t s="15">and oil is Chochmah S timaah, which is above the revelation of Binah and also above the revelation of Chochmah,</t>
    <t s="16">and is unfit for drinking.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="14">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The altar's dedication was through anointing with oil, representing Chochmah S timaah, and the addition of spices in the anointing oil alludes to the level of smell, which is even higher than oil and relates to Torah's hidden essence that nevertheless issues in practical law.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">8)</t>
    <t s="1">And this is that the dedication of the altar was by anointing it with the anointing oil,</t>
    <t s="2">for by drawing into it from the aspect of Chochmah S timaah</t>
    <t s="3">(the Chochmah that is in Kesser),</t>
    <t s="4">through this there was also drawn the power for the burning of the offerings and for the libation of wine of Binah and the libation of water of Chochmah48.</t>
    <t s="5">And the maamar adds48,</t>
    <t s="6">that in the anointing oil there were spices49,</t>
    <t s="7">the matter of smell,</t>
    <t s="8">which is even higher than oil.</t>
    <t s="9">And the explanation of this may be said,</t>
    <t s="10">that oil,</t>
    <t s="11">although it is above taste and human pleasure, to the point that it is unfit for drinking,</t>
    <t s="12">is still grasped by touch.</t>
    <t s="13">But smell is not grasped by touch,</t>
    <t s="14">and furthermore,</t>
    <t s="15">smell is50</t>
    <t s="16">a thing from which the soul derives pleasure, not the body51.</t>
    <t s="17">And from this one may also understand regarding the levels of the wisdom of Torah, which are compared to oil and to smell,</t>
    <t s="18">that the Torah being compared to oil refers, as above, to the secrets of secrets,</t>
    <t s="19">which even they</t>
    <t s="20">(the secrets of secrets)</t>
    <t s="21">come in intellectual revelation,</t>
    <t s="22">to the point that they are clothed in letters.</t>
    <t s="23">But the matter of smell in Torah is entirely above comprehension.</t>
    <t s="24">Nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="25">just as smell,</t>
    <t s="26">although it is a thing from which the soul derives pleasure and not the body,</t>
    <t s="27">it is known52</t>
    <t s="28">that through a strong smell one restores the soul that has been drawn into revelation in the body,</t>
    <t s="29">similarly it may be said regarding the matter of smell in Torah,</t>
    <t s="30">that it is drawn into actual practical ruling,</t>
    <t s="31">to the point that Moshiach will "smell and judge"53,</t>
    <t s="32">for the aspect of smell in him will be drawn into actual practical ruling</t>
    <t s="33">("smell and judge"),</t>
    <t s="34">except that the reason for the ruling is entirely above intellect.</t>
    <t s="35">And it may be said that this is like "Shav was silent"54</t>
    <t s="36">and nevertheless did not retract55,</t>
    <t s="37">for although this was for him a level of vision of Chochmah that was not revealed in intellect at all,</t>
    <t s="38">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="39">based on this vision</t>
    <t s="40">(which is above intellect)</t>
    <t s="41">he issued an actual practical ruling.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
